name: Cloud Security Alliance AI Controls Matrix (AICM), built on the CSA Cloud Controls Matrix (CCM v4)
description: The CSA AI Controls Matrix (AICM v1.0, released 2025-07-10) is an industry-consensus AI control framework with 243 control objectives across 18 domains — 17 carried from the CSA Cloud Controls Matrix (CCM v4) plus a new AI-specific Model Security (MDS) domain of 13 controls — and ships with an AI-CAIQ, implementation and auditing guidelines, and mappings to ISO 42001, ISO 27001, NIST AI RMF, BSI AIC4 and the EU AI Act. It is current as of mid-2025 and actively maintained. AGENT-RESPONSIBILITY-BOUNDARY CAVEAT: AKSI controls map to the runtime/inference-time slice (agent identity, action authori
jurisdiction: International (industry consensus standard; maps to ISO 42001, ISO 27001, NIST AI RMF 1.0, BSI AIC4, EU AI Act)
regime_version: AICM v1.0 (released 2025-07-10; controls/guidance refreshed through late 2025, sometimes labeled v1.0.x); CCM v4.0

GOV-01.framework_reference: IAM-19 (Agent Access Restriction) requires restricting/governing the access an AI agent identity holds. GOV-02 names an accountable owner per AI system for operation/risk/remediation, satisfying the agent-owned slice o

GOV-03.framework_reference: GRC governance/risk program requires risk-tolerance and policy baselines; GRC-15 (Human Supervision) presumes defined thresholds at which autonomous AI action requires oversight. GOV-03 defines autonomy limits + escalation thresholds in policy before autonomous action. Org-wide risk-program elements

GOV-04.framework_reference: GRC-15 (Human Supervision) requires human oversight/intervention over autonomous AI decisions. GOV-04 provides human review/approval context + decision accountability for sensitive actions/exceptions, which fully covers the agent-runtime slice of human supervision. Title confirmed by AICM narrative

GOV-05.framework_reference: GRC-09 (Acceptable Use of the AI Service) defines permitted/prohibited uses; DSP policies require purpose-bound, lawful data handling. GOV-05 binds actions/data-uses to declared purpose, contract limits, legal basis, consent and prohibited-use policy — the agent-owned slice of acceptable-use + lawfu

GOV-07.framework_reference: GRC-13 (Explainability Requirement) and acceptable-use disclosure plus STA transparency/accountability obligations require disclosures and affected-party transparency. PR-01.framework_reference: AIS-11 (Agents Security Boundaries) and IAM-19 (Agent Access Restriction) require constraining which actions an agent may take; GRC-15 gates sensitive actions to human supervision. PR-02.framework_reference: IAM-19 (Agent Access Restriction) requires least-privilege restriction of agent access; AIS-11 (Agents Security Boundaries) requires enforced action/permission boundaries. PR-02 enforces explicit least-privilege scopes per session + per action — squarely the agent permission-scope-enforcement slice.

PR-03.framework_reference: MDS-08 (Model Integrity Checks), MDS-09 (Model Signing/Ownership Verification), MDS-13 (Secure Model Format) and MDS-02 (Model Artifact Scanning) require verifying model/tool artifacts against trusted baselines. PR-03 verifies tool descriptors/model artifacts/execution surfaces vs trusted baselines

PR-10 gives persistent memory/retrieved context/shared task state provenance, integrity checks and quarantine (RAG/memory poisoning) — the agent memory/context-integrity

PR-11.framework_reference: DSP (Data Security & Privacy Lifecycle) requires data retention, secure disposal and lifecycle controls. RS-01.framework_reference: SEF (Security Incident Management / Events & Failures) requires defined incident response actions; TVM-11 (Guardrails) enables automated policy enforcement. RS-01 executes predefined policy responses when evidence crosses control/classification/overlay thresholds — the agent automated-response slice

RS-02.framework_reference: MDS-11 (Model Failure) handling, TVM-11 (Guardrails) and AIS-11 (Agents Security Boundaries) require the ability to halt/contain/degrade misbehaving AI; SEF provides incident containment. RS-02 blocks/quarantines/degrades/halts agents/tools/memory/credentials/actions on risk conditions (kill switch)

RS-03.framework_reference: SEF (Security Incident Management) requires incident escalation/reporting; GRC-15 (Human Supervision) routes exceptions to humans.
